rules.rule: Do not re-verify whether the Korea trip savings events exist in PocketSmith; they have already been confirmed live.
Never upload films.
Do not rebuild the Kurva S files.
Do not call `pipeline_update` with stage `upload` during a film session.
Do not implement the :base+15 SSH+SFTP channel (libssh, curve25519, ed25519) in the Switch port.
Do not pursue further reverse-engineering follow-up on the TIER5-B1 Capabilities advertisement axis; it is closed.
Do not search for a port for ComChan, since it has no socket.
Do not migrate the WebRTC stack to libdatachannel to work around the Switch freeze bug.
For the Switch port, do not implement QUIC support.
Never scrape the EAN-Search public site, because its terms forbid automated queries and it has bot protection.
Never work around a Cloudflare challenge from CeX.
Have the user confirm the final game match before accepting it.
Always target the Development branch when opening a GitHub PR, never main.
When opening a pull request, always target the Development branch for testing, never main.
Never bump the major version on your own initiative under any circumstances.
Only commit or push changes when explicitly asked to do so.
Never commit META_APP_TOKEN, MB_KEY, or other secrets to git.
Do not release or bypass the podiumd-minikube cluster-lock (.minikube-lock) or the kees00 lease podiumd-tests-lock.
Apply translations only after the user approves them, either with a go-ahead or with specific overrides.
Ask the user for confirmation before running kubectl apply, delete, patch, rollout restart, or exec.
Ask the user for confirmation before running argocd app sync, delete, or set.
Stop and ask the user before merging PRs.
Compact the Windows vhdx (which requires `wsl --shutdown`) only when no hook is running.
Never merge the PR yourself; leave review and merging to the user.
Only execute a commit when the user asks for it.
